Prepkin · mascot research, part two · 4 September 2026 · picks locked

Should different people get different kin?

You asked whether to run different mascots for different age groups and genders. The short answer from the market: yes to a roster, no to the labels. Every number below links to its source.

Verdict. The brands that win 16 to 24 run one hero plus a small roster, and let people sort themselves onto lanes that are dressed as personality, never as "for boys" or "for teens". Sanrio built Kuromi to catch the teens Hello Kitty was losing. Duolingo built a cast and Lily became the teen favourite while Duo stayed the brand. Pop Mart runs five IPs with no single hero and Labubu is 38% of revenue.

Two cautions. Every habit app at your team size ships one mascot plus cosmetics. And nobody has published proof that species choice raises retention. So: keep Sprout as the hero, add lanes one at a time, never label them, and let the first-run pick tell you who wants what.

What actually differs by gender and age

FindingNumbersSourceWhat it means for kin
Women respond more strongly to cutenessWomen 19 to 26 discriminate infant cuteness far better than men. The gap tracks hormones and closes after menopause.Sprengelmeyer 2009, Psychological Science StrongA very soft default kin will skew female. Real, not a stereotype.
Men lean competition, women lean completion and fantasy1.25M gamers. Completion is top three for every age and gender. Competition peaks at 13 to 25 and drops after.Quantic Foundry StrongCollecting works for everyone. Leagues and rank pull men at exactly your age.
ColourBlue is the universal favourite. Women shift a little toward red and pink within it. Held in the UK and China.Hurlbert and Ling 2007 StrongOffer both. Never gate a coat by gender.
Gen Z rejects gendered marketing81% say gender defines a person less than before. 59% of women 13 to 35 want brands to stop gendering messages.AMA, citing JWT and YPulse EstimateThe split can exist. The label cannot.
Aspirational ageTeens want products aimed a few years older. The aspirational age sits around 21.Trade concept, Advertising Week WeakDesign the whole app for 21. A 16 year old will reach up. A 21 year old will not reach down.
Teen cuteness response is weaker than adults'Baby-schema liking in adolescents exists but is weaker. Single study, n=76.Luo 2020 WeakSweetness alone lands worse at 16 than at 26. Attitude matters at 16.
Kidult spend is now gender-balanced18+ toy spend $1.8B in Q1 2025, up 12%. Growth split evenly by gender.Circana StrongMen buy cute things now. They buy the ones with an edge.

What it costs

  • No app at your size branches species. Finch, Focus Friend, Forest, Fabulous and Duolingo all ship one mascot plus cosmetics. None reports a business reason to add species. (Tubefilter, Finch wiki)
  • The one company that split by gender built separate apps. Outfit7 runs seven studios to keep the Talking Tom family alive. That is the price of full characters.
  • Nobody has measured species choice against retention. The strongest documented retention lever in this space is mascot writing: a personalised Duo message lifted day-14 retention 7.2% in one case study (secondary source).
  • Your cheap multiplier already exists. A look like Ninja sits on the same rig and changes the lane for a fraction of a new species. The badge and coat systems are the same trick.

What I'd do: one hero, three lanes, no labels

Sprout stays the face of the app. Each lane is a taste, not a demographic. Two of the three already exist in the Sprout repo. The first-run "pick three" screen shows one from each lane and logs the choice, which gives you real age and gender data within a month instead of a guess now.

Lane 1 · Soft · the hero

Sprout

Round, warm, blush. The Finch and Cinnamoroll register. Skews female by the cuteness science. Fine. That is the hero's job.

Cost: built. Apply the tone and eye moves from part one.

Lane 2 · Cool · creature · locked

Sail, redrawn

George picked this ocean-grey, half-lidded manta on 4 Sept over the old sky-blue rig. Wide wings, a glide instead of a bob. The Pokémon-water-starter register. Reads competitive and unbothered. This is the lane the Quantic Foundry data says men 13 to 25 want.

Next: retrace this reference into the Sail rig in the Sprout repo, then coats, badges and iOS stills.

Lane 3 · Edge · attitude · locked

Orca and Axolotl

Both picked 4 Sept. The pear-shaped orca with half-lidded eyes, and the axolotl in two coats, lilac and rose. The Kuromi, Gudetama and Labubu register.

Next: two new types on the pear rig. Orca first, it shares Sprout's silhouette. Axolotl adds gill fronds as a separately outlined accessory.

  1. Never label a lane.No "for boys", no "teen", no pink and blue. Name them by personality like Sanrio and Pop Mart do. Gen Z data on gendered marketing, and the aspirational-age rule.
  2. Design everything for 21.Copy, tanks, badges. Aspirational age. A 16 year old reaches up. A 22 year old will not use a thing that feels 16.
  3. Ship lane 2 before lane 3.Sail is mostly built. It covers the competitive lane with the least new art.
  4. Put one of each lane in the first-run pick and log it.Age band and pick, nothing else. Every roster brand learned who picks what after the fact. You can learn it in a month.
  5. Use looks and badges as the cheap variety.Ninja on all three lanes. Blind-box coat drops. Cosmetics are what Finch, Focus Friend and Forest sell. Collecting is the one motivation every group shares.
  6. Do not go past three lanes this year.Outfit7 needed seven studios. Pop Mart's five IPs came one at a time over a decade.

What I could not verify

  • Which starter Pokémon, villager or Genshin twin different genders pick. Only fan polls exist.
  • Pop Mart buyer gender. Press numbers conflict (43 to 51% male vs 60% female).
  • Outfit7's per-app gender split and the Angela revenue figure. Third-party estimates only.
  • The Duolingo 7.2% retention lift. Secondary case study, no primary post found.
